text: It's so incredibly frustrating.  I am a longtime sim pilot (started with FSX/XPlane then P3D, then MSFS).  When nearly the topmost GPU on the recommended top-tier Intel CPU is having 'issues' with dropped frames... one surmises indeed MSFS is "The New Crysis". Just fried my patience to a crisp.  I wonder because I initially had an xBox account (but did all my flying on my PC) if on the 27th the game itself got confused.  My controllers are NOT supported on the XBox at all, but work just fine on my PC (or they used to prior to 27 Jul).  Very poor QA at MS/Asobo in my view.  I am aware that all the lighting, volumetric clouds, photogrammetry, and other 'features' is indeed a herculean task than can bring even the top tier hardware to a screeching stutter.  MS 'advertises' 4K for this game.  Not sure if that is all that realistic.  I have seen Xbox Series X drop into the mid-20's doing native 1440p renders shown at 4K after upscaling.  I tried a Corsair 5800 with a RTX 3070 on my LG OLED TV and it was a very 'meh' experience sad to say.   DX 12 "might" help but in and of itself, I don't think even DX12 is going to be the final answer.  In fairness, there is a LOT going on.  We have a secret dream that we'll find a sim that looks as good as flight does in real life... with smooth stutter-free presentation and real world flight-dynamics. text:
This game made me upgrade my 6 year old PC. I had no idea that 4.5Ghz was crap, as I thought Moore's Law was all but stalled these days. However, my old overclocked i5-3570K was a stuttering nightmare. At first, I assumed it was my GTX 970, so I went on eBay and bought a used GTX 1080. Nope. FS2020 still suffered a good five minutes of profound stuttering before clearing up.

My next thought, normally, would have been to try a fresh Windows format/install. But I had just done one a few weeks earlier, so I knew that wasn't the issue. 

All the reviews of the game assumed me my 16GB of system ram was enough. So that led me to the dreadful realization, it was simply time for a whole new system build.

Ryzen 9 3900x
32GB DDR4 3600
500GB PCIe Gen4 NVMe system drive
2TB PCIe Gen3 NVMe game drive
And that used GTX 1080

Stutters are all gone! The game loads up and is immediately ready to go. I get a playable 30fps on High Settings, 4K and 80% rendering.

Of course, the build is not done yet. I'm working hard to get my hands on an RTX 3080. But... that's proving difficult. lol
